evidence.quote: Mechanical alloying (MA) was carried out at ambient temperature using a Fretsch Pulverisette P-6 planetary ball mill in a hardened stainless steel container using 10 mm diameter stainless steel balls. For MA, the container was purged with Ar, and the powder to ball ratio was kept at 1:10 with 6 wt% ethanol as the process control agent, and run at a milling speed of 250 rpm for 50–150 h.
The powders were sintered under a vacuum of ∼2 × 10−3 Pa under a 35 kN load at a 400, 420 or 480 ◦C for 10 min. Samples were heated at 2 ◦C/s.

Bulk nano-crystalline Al–1Fe–0.5Zr alloys fabricated by mechanical alloying and spark plasma sintering exhibited high compressive yield strength of 854 MPa with a plastic strain of 19% at room temperature and 455 MPa and 16.7% at 250 ◦C.

The nanocrystalline region contained a very ﬁne distribution of intermetallic particles, which is likely to suppress the grain coarsening during the SPS process by pinning the grain boundaries of the nano-crystalline Al grains.

The microstructure characterization results indicate that the high strength obtained in the present sample is mainly due to the ﬁne grained structure, and the dispersion of the intermetallic phases such as Al6Fe and Al3Zr.
